details: Owner, verbatim: "заведи пункт про перенос bash в python". Bash behaves differently on macOS (bash 3.2, BSD tools): on 24 Oct the project template's check failed on a Mac because it called `timeout` and `md5sum`, which macOS lacks. Two languages also mean two ways to test and two sets of traps.
failing_case: 24 Oct: templates/bin-check called `timeout`/`md5sum` (GNU-only), so the first check of a new project on a Mac failed; relay has 3,438 lines of bash, 2,564 of them hook test suites.
pass_cases: After the move, the gate runs the same cases (same count) from Python; no .sh file under plugins/ holds more than a few lines of wrapper; the gate passes on macOS with no GNU tools on PATH.
reason: tests/test_bin_check_portable.py (13 tests on a PATH without timeout/md5sum) pass; 13 of them fail against the old bash template at 2414c373.
findings.summary: Hook tests and wrappers are bash, not portable Python

details: CONFIRMED by reading and line counts. The queue item's What has three parts: the hook test suites, the hook wrappers
("keep at most a few lines of exec python3"), and bin/ci plus templates/bin-check. The branch did the first (and
graders.test.sh); the commits stop at "hook_tests step no longer globs *.test.sh". The builder's own report says
"BUDGET SPENT (partial)". This is a promise of the item left undone, so HIGH. The owner may instead move the wrapper and
bin-check part to a new queue item (a scope cut only the owner can make); without that word it is open.
Size: 90 (guard-main.sh is the bulk; its tests already exist in Python and make the port checkable).
evidence: git log --oneline master..HEAD: 19 "Port <suite> hook tests" commits, one graders port, no hook or bin-check commit.
Builder report: "BUDGET SPENT (partial): ported 6 of 14 suites ...; remaining: ... hook wrappers, bin-check."
failing_case: After the change: plugins/relay/hooks/guard-main.sh has 148 code lines of bash (jq parsing, anchor and main-checkout
resolution, bindings read, the rules), plugins/relay/hooks/inject-addition.sh 55, templates/bin-check 78 (hash8 and
bound() fallbacks for md5sum/timeout). The item's pass case "no .sh file under plugins/ holds more than a few lines of
wrapper" fails for both hooks, and "bin/ci and templates/bin-check keep only what a shell must do" fails for bin-check.
Only the test suites (and graders.test.sh) moved.
fix_hint: Port guard-main.sh to plugins/relay/hooks/guard_main.py (it already shells out to kit/lib Python) and inject-addition.sh
likewise, leaving `exec python3 "$(dirname "$0")/<name>.py"`; move bin-check's bound/hash8 into a Python helper. Or, with
the owner's word, file that part as its own queue item and close this one on the tests alone.
pass_cases: 1. Every plugins/*/hooks/*.sh holds at most a few lines (e.g. <= 5 code lines) that exec python3 on a .py beside it;
guard-main.sh and inject-addition.sh included.
2. tests/test_hook_guard_main.py, test_hook_guard_diff.py, test_hook_check_mark.py (G cases) and
test_hook_inject_addition.py pass unchanged against the Python hooks (same verdicts, same golden output).
3. templates/bin-check keeps no hash or timeout logic in bash (the bound/hash8 work is Python); the check-contract suite
still passes against the eval fixture.
4. With a PATH that holds no GNU coreutils (no timeout, no md5sum), the guard and bin-check still work.
reason: Hooks are 1-2 line wrappers; templates/bin-check is stdlib Python (hashlib, subprocess timeout); tests/test_bin_check_portable.py and test_template_python_gate.py pass.
findings.summary: the hook wrappers and templates/bin-check are still logic-bearing bash; the item's What and its pass case are not met

details: CONFIRMED by counting (old: ran each master suite and counted ^ok lines; new: grep -c 'def test_'). Every case I
name-checked is still asserted, so nothing is lost in coverage; what is lost is per-case reporting and the count the
item names as its pass case. guard-main and guard-diff already collect all failures before asserting; ledger,
check-mark, inject-addition, kit, packet, packet-stacks, spec-check and merge stop at the first failed assert.
Size: 45 (wrap each old case in self.subTest(<old name>) in the merged methods).
evidence: ports: budget 6, check_contract 8, check_mark 22, flow_stage 3, guard_diff 1, guard_main 6, inject_addition 10,
kit_name 1, kit 9, ledger 11, merge 44, packet_stacks 4, packet 8, route_guard 12, shim 7, spec_check 3 (sum 155)
tests/test_hook_inject_addition.py:118-122 loops over prompts with plain assertIn/assertEqual.
failing_case: The quick gate on master counted 743 passing hook cases (route-guard 12, ledger 25, check-mark 80, guard-main 204,
inject-addition 54, merge 99, packet 97, ...). The ports hold 155 test methods (ledger 11, check-mark 22, inject-addition 10,
packet 8, spec-check 3, guard-main 6). Several old cases now sit in one method with plain asserts, e.g.
tests/test_hook_inject_addition.py test_prompt loops over "/openspec:plan", "  /openspec:plan x", then the negative
prompts: if "  /openspec:plan x" (leading spaces) breaks, the method stops there and the eight negative prompt cases
are not run or reported; the gate shows 1 failure where bash showed each failing case by name. The item asked "Keep the
test cases and their names" and "the gate runs the same cases (same count)".
fix_hint: In each merged method, run each old case under `with self.subTest("<old case name>"):` so a failure names it and the rest
still run; the per-case names then appear in a failing run as they did in bash.
pass_cases: 1. Break one case inside a multi-case method (e.g. make inject-addition ignore leading spaces): the run reports that case
by its old name AND still runs and reports the later cases of the same method.
2. The number of cases the gate reports for the hook suites equals the old 743 (subtests or one method per case),
or the report states the mapping old-name -> test id for every case.
3. All suites still pass on the unchanged hooks.
4. guard-main keeps reporting every wrong verdict at once (it already collects `bad`), as today.
reason: tests/test_hook_soft_cases.py passes; SoftCases from tests/hook_helpers.py is used in all merged suites so later cases still run and each failure is named; measured case table in the fixer report shows no suite runs fewer cases than bash.
findings.summary: 743 named cases became 155 test methods: one failing case hides the rest of its method, and the item's 'same count' is not met

details: CONFIRMED by reading lib/relay_ci.py hook_tests (no glob) and outcome(). Correct today (Ran N does not change with
RELAY_QUICK because guard_main defines the same methods), so LOW: a regression guard that guards nothing.
failing_case: test_a_full_run_is_probed_with_its_hook_suites_in_full plants plugins/x/tests/a.test.sh that prints one or two ok lines
depending on RELAY_QUICK. hook_tests now runs only tests/hooks_live.py, so the file is never run and outcome()'s
"hook cases ok" is 0 in both runs. Delete the `not env.get("RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS")` condition in Ci.lib_tests
(lib/relay_ci.py:283): the test still passes. outcome() (lib/relay_ci.py:58-63) still counts hook-tests.log ok lines,
which no step writes outside hooks_live (skipped), so that line is always "hook cases ok: 0".
fix_hint: Rewrite the planted suite as tests/test_x.py with a RELAY_QUICK-dependent method, and drop the hook-case count from outcome().
pass_cases: 1. A planted tests/test_x.py whose number of tests depends on RELAY_QUICK (e.g. a method defined only when it is not "1"):
a full outer gate ends with "ci: inert ok"; with the RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS condition removed from lib_tests it ends
"ci: inert FAILED".
2. outcome() no longer reports a hook-case count that no step can produce (or counts something a step still writes).
3. test_ci_hook_tests keeps passing.
reason: tests/test_gate.py:465-472 now plants tests/test_x.py with a RELAY_QUICK-dependent test; test_ci_hook_tests passes.
findings.summary: the inert hook-case test now passes with the behaviour disabled: no step runs plugins/x/tests/a.test.sh any more
